summary: The 2026 LLM landscape is dominated by a handful of frontier families — OpenAI's GPT-5 line, Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini, and Meta's open-weight Llama — with Chinese labs (DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen) and Mistral providing strong open or low-cost alternatives. Enterprise adoption is increasingly mediated through cloud aggregators (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx), which significantly amplifies real-world usage of models available on multiple platforms. Because the live research data confirms only a subset of exact model names, this ranking is limited to models that can be verified as publicly available today and names models conservatively.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: The default workhorse model across OpenAI's API and a first-class option on Azure OpenAI, giving it the broadest combined direct-API and enterprise-aggregator reach of any model.
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications and multimodal assistants

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Research notes it matches Opus-level performance at Sonnet pricing (shipped Feb 17), and it is available across AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and direct API, driving heavy enterprise and coding adoption.
models.best_for: Agentic coding workflows and enterprise automation

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: A high-volume, low-cost model with large context, natively distributed through Google Vertex AI and the Gemini API, giving it enormous reach among cost-sensitive developers.
models.best_for: High-throughput, cost-sensitive applications with long context

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Described in the research as the 'context window king'; available via Vertex AI and the Gemini API, it is a leading choice for long-document and large-codebase enterprise tasks.

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: A 671B-parameter MoE reasoning model cited as the cheapest frontier-class model at $0.55/$2.19 per 1M tokens, with heavy HuggingFace downloads and growing availability on aggregators like AWS Bedrock and Azure.
strengths: Extremely low cost for frontier performance
models.best_for: Cost-efficient reasoning, math, and algorithmic problem solving

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: Meta's most-downloaded open-weight instruct model, ubiquitous on HuggingFace and offered across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx, making it the default open-weights enterprise choice.

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: The general-purpose counterpart to R1, widely adopted for delivering near-frontier quality at a fraction of the cost and heavily downloaded on HuggingFace.
strengths: Strong general performance at low cost

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's fast, low-cost tier available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and direct API, widely used for high-volume classification, routing, and lightweight agent tasks.

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: Alibaba's flagship open-weights MoE model with strong HuggingFace adoption and rapidly growing use in Asian markets and among open-source developers.
models.best_for: Multilingual and open-weights applications, especially in Asian markets

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Mistral's European flagship, available via its own API plus AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Google Vertex AI, favored for data-residency-conscious enterprise deployments in Europe.
models.best_for: European enterprise deployments with data-residency requirements
